text.p: - Slovenian ski-jumper Primoz Peterka resumed his leading overall position in the World Cup after winning third and first place in two ski-flying events in Kulm, Austria at the weekend.

- Slovenian prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek will continue coalition talks with parliamentary parties this week, after his previous line-up was refused. He must present his new candidates to parliament by February 17.
- President Milan Kucan said parliament's rejection of Drnovsek's government line-up last Thursday was not unexpected, due to the inflexibility of the parties during talks.
- Slovenian firms have received 100 quality certificates ISO 9001. The last company that received the certificate was constructor SCT.

- Slovenian railways said they had the capacity to carry up to eight times the current amount of ecologically harmful material (1.1 million tonnes) transferred through Slovenia. Last year eight leaks were found in cisterns containing dangerous materials.

- Marjan Podobnik, president of the conservative People's Party said he hoped prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek would not try to propose the same ministerial candidates again as support could fall to 40 votes from 45 last Thursday.

- A decision on whether the Republika newspaper will be published daily or weekly is expected to be taken next week, the paper's chief editor said. Republika stopped publication on Friday due to financial troubles.
- Slovenia's privatisation agency said that 1,347 companies have already completed privatisation, while 906 more companies are still in the process of being privatised.
